stem: An insurance claims company's workflow team is building a claims-approval process that must run for up to several months per claim, with full execution history retained for audits.

choices.text: A Step Functions Express workflow, since it supports a much higher event rate
Chain Amazon SQS delay queues between the approval steps, with each queue holding the claim until the next stage begins
Chain several Step Functions Express workflows together, starting the next one when the previous one finishes
A Step Functions Standard workflow, which runs up to a year and keeps full execution history

rationale: A Step Functions Standard workflow gives exactly-once execution, runs for up to a year, and keeps full execution history for auditing, which matches a months-long, auditable claims-approval process. An Express workflow trades that away for a much higher event rate, but it runs for at most five minutes, far short of the months this process needs. Chaining SQS delay queues between steps can sequence work, but a queue's maximum retention is 14 days, nowhere near the several months a claim may need to wait between stages, and a queue keeps no execution history for an audit. Chaining several Express workflows together still caps each individual workflow at five minutes and creates a separate execution record for each link in the chain instead of the single, continuous, fully auditable execution a Standard workflow provides.
